CausalChain: BNCT induces high‐LET radiation → causes targeted tumor cell death and release of tumor antigens/DAMPs → upregulates local inflammation and antigen presentation → creates an immunogenic microenvironment → administration of immune adjuvants or checkpoint inhibitors lifts immune suppression → potentiates T-cell mediated systemic anti-tumor responses → potential abscopal effects and improved overall therapeutic efficacy.
Hypothesis: Integrating BNCT with immune-modulatory strategies—either via local adjuvant delivery or systemic immune checkpoint blockade—will synergistically enhance both local tumor ablation and systemic anti-tumor immunity, converting immunologically ‘cold’ tumors into ‘hot’ ones and thereby improving overall treatment outcomes.
Abstract: Boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT) is emerging as a promising modality for the selective ablation of tumor cells through high linear-energy-transfer reactions. Beyond its direct cytotoxic effects, BNCT appears to cause immunogenic cell death, leading to the release of tumor antigens and damage‐associated molecular patterns that could prime the immune system. This review highlights opportunities to enhance BNCT’s therapeutic efficacy by integrating it with immune-modulatory agents. Here, we propose that combining BNCT with local administration of immune adjuvants or systemic immune checkpoint inhibitors may convert immunologically ‘cold’ tumors into ‘hot’ ones, thereby potentiating both local tumor control and systemic abscopal effects. This hypothesis suggests a novel multi-modality approach that leverages BNCT-induced tumor immunogenicity to enhance overall treatment outcomes in refractory and metastatic malignancies.
